newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS-EDP sale gives Portugal bumper payday.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-EDP sale gives Portugal bumper payday.

text.p: Portugal had its biggest single payday from privatisations on Monday, picking up over $2 billion for 30 percent stake in utility concern EDP- Electricidade de Portugal.
The 179 million shares on offer were priced at 2,250 escudos, the top of the pre-sale range set by the Socialist government, the Lisbon bourse announced.

International institutional concerns, banks, investment and pension funds, joined ordinary Portuguese investors in pouring money into the privatisation, which outstripped the earlier sale of stakes in Portugal Telecom.
Demand from local investors alone was some 37 times the 97 million shares set aside for them. The remainder of the stock went to foreign institutions, mostly in the United States and Britain.
"This operation can be considered a great success...EDP is going to end up with the best possible range of international investors," a delighted company chairman Antonio de Almeida told journalists.

Analysts expect the price of shares in EDP, which will become the largest stock on the bourse, to soar after the sale as disappointed institutional investors seek to buy on the market the stock they failed to get at the privatisation.

The company posted a 26 percent rise in profit in 1996 to 81 billion escudos and analysts are optimistic about its prospects as demand for electricity in Portugal, still one of Europe's poorest countries, grows rapidly.

"The shares will probably perform very well. Demand has been fantastically high and you could see the shares going up by about 30 percent during the next week," Diego Hernando, chief economist at Lisbon brokers Midas, told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).
Some analysts said that demand from frustrated investors could propel the stock towards 2,700, or even 3,000 escudos soon after its debut on the Lisbon bourse on Tuesday.
The Lisbon bourse has been one of Europe's best performing stock markets over the past 18 months, with a string of privatisations helping to boost liquidity.

The market was given an additional boost recently by news that Morgan Stanley Capital International, whose indices are a sort of Bible to the international investor, was going to promote the market from emerging to developed before the end of the year.
The new ranking will automatically draw in money from big international investment funds, analysts say.
